title: Work IQ: business skills for agents through Work IQ MCP
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap record and current Microsoft documentation. The updated Sales agent article still supports the Allowed MCP Clients path, and the Dataverse reference supports the PATCH operation, entity key and Boolean setting despite the automatic text-match warning.

claims.claim: Default enablement for eligible new environments starts September 30, 2026.
claims.quote: Starting September 30, 2026, Microsoft turns on these capabilities by default for all new environments that aren't listed as exceptions in this article.

claims.claim: Default enablement for eligible existing environments starts in November 2026.
claims.quote: Starting in November 2026, Microsoft turns on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptions.

claims.claim: The automatic default applies to public production environments, subject to the listed exceptions.
claims.quote: The default applies to public production environments created for new or existing tenants. The following environments are exceptions:

claims.claim: EU and EFTA environments are exceptions to current default enablement.
claims.quote:
The following environments are exceptions:

- European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments

claims.claim: Microsoft plans default enablement for EU and EFTA environments at general availability rather than publishing an exact date.
claims.quote: Microsoft plans to enable environments provisioned in the European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments when the feature becomes generally available.

claims.claim: During public preview, EU and EFTA customers can turn on Work IQ using the corresponding Microsoft 365 admin center setting.
claims.quote: During public preview, customers can turn on Work IQ by using the corresponding setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: Government-related environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Trial, sandbox and developer environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: Nonproduction environments: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.claim: Work IQ must be enabled in the Dataverse environment for business skills to be used there.
claims.quote: The Work IQ setting turns on business skills, semantic modeling, and access to Dataverse data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research, and Agent Builder. If you turn off this setting, these features aren't available in the environment.

claims.claim: Agent skill selection is probabilistic.

claims.claim: Skill access controls govern who can read skill instructions and resources.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Skill creation, modification and use are governed through Dataverse ownership, sharing and security roles.
claims.quote: Governance—Control who can create, modify, and use business skills through ownership, sharing, and Dataverse security roles.

claims.claim: Security-role sharing requires both the selected Dataverse role and Skill Sharing Role.
claims.quote: Users who access a skill through a Dataverse security role must have both the selected role and the Skill Sharing Role security role.

claims.claim: General access and direct access are separate skill-sharing methods.
claims.quote:
General access—Makes the skill available to everyone in the environment.
Direct access—Shares the skill with specific users or groups and lets you choose whether they can view or edit the skill.

claims.claim: Activating an updated skill changes the active instructions available to agents.
claims.quote: Save and activate | Makes your changes the active version, including its associated resources. The previous active version remains in version history.

claims.claim: Saving an edited working copy alone does not change the active version.
claims.quote: Save | Saves your working copy without changing the version agents use. A new skill remains inactive. If the skill already has an active version, that version stays active.

claims.claim: Environment Work IQ participation is configured in Power Platform admin center at Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Power Platform admin center.
Select Manage, and select the environment.
Select Settings > Product > Features.
Locate Work IQ.
Turn on Work IQ if it's currently off.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API equivalent for the environment Work IQ switch at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ environment enable Work IQ Power Platform API PowerShell pac admin organization setting; Work IQ Enable organization PowerShell API Power Platform; Work IQ pac admin PowerShell. Read manage-participation, default-settings, quickstart and pac admin excerpts; no switch API found.

claims.claim: Tenant Copilot access is configured in Microsoft 365 admin center at Copilot > Settings > View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation pane, select Copilot > Settings.
In Copilot settings, select View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API equivalent for the tenant Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Business Applications data in Work IQ" "Graph" API setting. Read default-settings and manage-ai-experience-access; reviewed Graph search results, Dataverse intelligence and compliance excerpts. No API for this tenant audience setting found.

claims.claim: Allowed MCP Clients is reached in Power Platform admin center through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Advanced Settings > Allowed MCP Clients.
claims.quote:
Go to Manage > Environments, and then select the environment.
In the Dataverse Model Context Protocol section, select Go to Advanced Settings.
In Advanced Settings > Allowed MCP Clients, open Enterprise Copilot Platform

claims.claim: PATCH [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients({allowedmcpclientid}) with body {"isenabled": false} disables the selected allowed MCP client.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients; Primary key: allowedmcpclientid; Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE; isenabled | Edm.Boolean | Display name: Is Enabled; 1 | Yes; 0 | No

claims.claim: Tenant Work IQ MCP server access can be blocked in Microsoft 365 admin center at Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Select Agents > Tools.
Select Work IQ MCP.
Review its current availability.
To block access to the server, select Block.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API equivalent for the tenant Work IQ MCP server availability setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" "block" "Graph" API; Work IQ MCP availability Microsoft Graph beta admin tools block. Read manage-ai-experience-access and returned MCP policy, migration and Agent 365 excerpts. No API for the server availability switch found.

claims.claim: The tenant setting cascades over environment features.
claims.quote:
You manage Business Applications in Work IQ through a cascading set of settings at three levels:
If you turn off this setting, data isn't shared between Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse, even if an app is configured to share data.

claims.claim: In Power Apps, selecting a skill and then Share opens skill sharing.
claims.quote: Select a skill, and then select Share from the command bar or the three-dot menu

claims.claim: Manage access shows skill access and allows access levels to be changed or access removed.
claims.quote: Select Manage access to review who has access, change access levels, or remove access.

claims.claim: The Dataverse CLI documents dataverse mcp allow <appId> to allow an application as a Dataverse MCP client.
claims.quote:
Ensure that a Microsoft Entra application is in the Dataverse MCP allowed clients list for the current profile's environment.
dataverse mcp allow <appId> [options]
The <appId> argument is the application (client) ID to allow, as a GUID.
